But. if the goal is to scare people away. from crime by publicly displaying death. , is that really effective? Based on. current research, it likely is not. The. U.S. National Research Council reviewed. decades of related studies and. concluded that existing research cannot. prove whether the death penalty. increases, decreases, or has no effect. on murder rates. Research institutions. under the Department of Justice have. also pointed out that what truly serves. as a deterrent is the likelihood of. being caught, not the severity of the. punishment. July found that 59%believe it does not. deter serious crime. Some former. officials also worry that a livestream. would package Hassan as a martyr,. serving as a recruitment tool. Moreover. , history has shown that public. executions do not necessarily produce. the results governments expect. During. early public executions in the U.S.,. people would even bring picnics to. watch; it only made people numb to. violence and emboldened criminals,. which is why states began moving. executions into prisons starting in the. 1820s. If public executions could. really deter crime, why were they moved. inside prisons in the first place? Looking back at Taiwan, our death. penalty is carried out by firing squad. within detention centers, and it is not. open to the public. As mentioned. earlier, nearly 60%of Americans believe. the death penalty cannot deter serious. crime, but polls in Taiwan show about. 80%of the public supports it, with many. believing it can deter crime and. maintain order. There is a significant. gap here compared to American public. opinion, so I’d like to ask: what is. your main reason for supporting the. death penalty? Is it because you. believe those who commit heinous crimes. should pay the price, or because you. believe the death penalty truly deters. crime? 摘要

八旬老婦遭驅離逝世引爆全國怒火

作者指出，西班牙馬德里一位87歲的老婦人瑪麗．卡門（Mari Carmen）在同一間公寓生活了長達70年且按時繳租，卻因法規修改面臨強制遷離。歷經多年訴訟與抗爭後，她在第四次驅逐行動中被擔架抬上救護車送醫，不久後在醫院過世。這場悲劇引爆西班牙全國性的強烈抗議，抗議者佔領太陽門廣場要求政府立法禁止在無安置方案下驅逐房客，更促使首相解散國會提前大選。

歷史遺留的「舊租約」與法律角力

作者回溯源頭，瑪麗．卡門自1956年佛朗哥獨裁時期便與父母入住，合約屬於早期受法律保障、租金極低且可世代繼承的「舊租約」。然而，1994年西班牙修法限制繼承次數與期限。當公寓產權於近年轉賣給不動產公司後，新房東要求調漲至她無法負擔的租金並提起訴訟。法院最終判定繼承期限已過而判房東勝訴，儘管各方在悲劇發生前夕曾達成協議讓她以原本租金重返公寓，但她已來不及回家。

作者進一步探討民眾憤怒背後的深層住房危機。首先是薪資完全追不上房價，過去十年間工資僅成長30%，房價與租金漲幅卻高達80%以上，單身租客租金甚至吃掉過半收入；其次是供給嚴重不足，2008年金融海嘯後營建業萎縮，加上社會住宅比例僅佔約1.5%至1.7%，遠低於歐盟平均，預估至2028年將面臨高達百萬戶的住宅缺口。
